## Traffic Status — live ops wall
**Every panel is real-time** (VictoriaMetrics `voip-metrics-vm` — Kamailio `xhttp_prom` + the FreeSWITCH ESL exporter, scraped ~15s), so this reflects the fleet as it is **right now**, not the retrospective CDR view (all CDR-delayed volume/ASR/carrier-split/hangup analytics moved to **Call Quality**). **CPS** = live seizures/sec; **concurrent calls** = FreeSWITCH `calls_active` (live) with a **high-water-mark** ladder (1h/24h/7d/30d, per zone vs the 8K upgrade trigger, channels per node vs max-sessions 10,000) built on the burst-safe 30s-peak recording rules (`noc_concurrency`, fill in from rule deploy); **dialogs** = Kamailio signaling concurrency; **Live ASR / failure %** = Kamailio INVITE reply-class rates over 5m. Carrier UP/DOWN is the only non-VM source — the SBCs' Kamailio-dispatcher OPTIONS probes via `carrier_trunk_health` (`voip-cdr-pg`), poller-fresh (~3–15s), not call-derived. `zone` label comes from `external_labels`; the **Zone** picker (`$zonere`) filters the SBC/dialog/ASR selectors. **Carriers:** Bandwidth Dallas (primary) · Bandwidth LA (secondary) · `local` = on-net. **Active SBC per zone** (top row — LEFT tile of each zone pair) = the NLB election per zone, decided by per-SBC scrape LIVENESS (present_over_time of an always-exported Kamailio gauge, 2m window) — with failover-ratio=0 the primary serves whenever its Kamailio is alive, so: green = primary ACTIVE (normal, even at zero traffic) · orange = ⚠ ON STANDBY (primary dark, standby serving) · red = ZONE DARK (both dark). Election truth at all times — it does NOT depend on call volume; per-SBC volume lives in 'Dialogs per SBC — now' + 'CPS per SBC (1m rate)'. **Active FS per zone** (top row — RIGHT tile of each zone pair) = the MEDIA election per zone, decided by the FS ESL exporter's own health gauge (last_over_time of freeswitch_esl_scrape_ok, 2m — VALUE-aware, so a dead FS container on a live VM reads unhealthy, not merely absent). Kamailio dispatcher priority selection (alg 8, FS-1 prio 10 / FS-2 prio 5) serves FS-1 whenever it is healthy, so: green = FS-1 ACTIVE (normal — a FLAT standby is BY DESIGN, this row is what separates 'standby idle' from 'broken') · orange = ⚠ FAILED OVER (FS-2 serving new calls) · red = MEDIA DOWN (both FS unhealthy — zone media dark). Per-FS volume lives in 'CPS per FreeSWITCH (1m rate)'.

panels.title: East · SBC (HA)
panels.description: NLB election truth for EAST (active/standby pair: poc-custom-voip = east-sbc-1 PRIMARY / kam-g2 = east-sbc-2 STANDBY), valid at ZERO traffic. With failover-ratio=0 the primary serves iff its Kamailio is alive — the /healthz fs_up component is common-mode (shared FreeSWITCH, fails BOTH SBCs together) so it never differentiates the pair — which makes per-SBC scrape liveness THE election signal: value = 1*(east-sbc-1 fresh) + 2*(east-sbc-1 stale AND east-sbc-2 fresh), freshness = present_over_time(kamailio_shmem_used_size{reporting_instance=...}[2m]) on an always-exported gauge. GREEN = primary serving (normal). ORANGE = FAILED OVER, standby serving (detection lag up to ~2m + refresh; the NLB itself flips in ~6s). RED 'ZONE DARK' = BOTH SBCs' metrics absent — zone outage OR metrics path down (vmagent/WAN/VictoriaMetrics): cross-check Infra Overview, the GCM 'SBC failover state' alert and gcloud backend-services get-health. Always shown regardless of the Zone filter. Runbook: docs/SBC_ACTIVE_STANDBY_RUNBOOK.md MAINTENANCE-AWARE (drain plane): a maintenance-drained SBC keeps exporting metrics, so raw scrape freshness alone would keep claiming it active — eligibility is now freshness AND NOT drained: kamailio_maint_drain{reporting_instance=...} (gauge refreshed every few seconds by the /healthz handler the NLB probes, [2m]-freshness-clamped, `or vector(0)`-guarded so a fully stopped kamailio reads 0 and the row degrades to the legacy DOWN/STANDBY states — a dead node can never fake MAINT). Encoding: value = 1*E1 + 2*E2*(1-E1) + 10*M1 + 20*M2 with E = fresh*(1-maint) — ones digit = elected eligible node (legacy semantics preserved exactly when neither SBC is drained), tens digits = maint bitmask. States: 0 = ZONE DARK (red, unchanged) | 1 = SBC-1 ACTIVE (green, unchanged) | 2 = ON STANDBY, SBC-2 serving after an UNPLANNED SBC-1 loss (orange, unchanged) | 12 = SBC-1 MAINT -> SBC-2 ACTIVE (yellow: PLANNED drain, standby serving — not a failover page) | 21 = SBC-1 ACTIVE with SBC-2 MAINT (green: primary serving normally but NO standby cover) | 30 = ZONE MAINT (yellow: BOTH SBCs drained — zone intentionally dark, distinct from red ZONE DARK) | 10 = SBC-1 MAINT + SBC-2 DOWN and 20 = SBC-2 MAINT + SBC-1 DOWN (red: the only non-drained SBC is dead — nobody can serve). Codes 11/22/31/32 are unreachable: a drained node is never eligible. Note: if a drained kamailio is then fully stopped for the maintenance work itself, its maint gauge goes stale within 2m and the row intentionally falls back to the legacy reading.

targets.expr: 1 * ((clamp_max(sum(present_over_time(kamailio_shmem_used_size{reporting_instance="east-sbc-1"}[2m])), 1) or vector(0)) * (1 - (clamp_max(max(last_over_time(kamailio_maint_drain{reporting_instance="east-sbc-1"}[2m])) or vector(0), 1)))) + 2 * ((clamp_max(sum(present_over_time(kamailio_shmem_used_size{reporting_instance="east-sbc-2"}[2m])), 1) or vector(0)) * (1 - (clamp_max(max(last_over_time(kamailio_maint_drain{reporting_instance="east-sbc-2"}[2m])) or vector(0), 1)))) * (1 - ((clamp_max(sum(present_over_time(kamailio_shmem_used_size{reporting_instance="east-sbc-1"}[2m])), 1) or vector(0)) * (1 - (clamp_max(max(last_over_time(kamailio_maint_drain{reporting_instance="east-sbc-1"}[2m])) or vector(0), 1))))) + 10 * (clamp_max(max(last_over_time(kamailio_maint_drain{reporting_instance="east-sbc-1"}[2m])) or vector(0), 1)) + 20 * (clamp_max(max(last_over_time(kamailio_maint_drain{reporting_instance="east-sbc-2"}[2m])) or vector(0), 1))

panels.description: Media (FreeSWITCH) election truth for EAST (strict active/standby pair: fs-media-v2 = FS-1 ACTIVE / east-fs-2 = FS-2 HOT STANDBY), valid at ZERO traffic — a standby FS showing flat/absent call metrics is BY DESIGN, and this panel is what separates 'standby idle' from 'broken'. panels.title: Inbound calls per $__interval — by zone
panels.description:
Calls OFFERED into the platform from carriers, counted at the SBC on each admitted initial INVITE (Kamailio `kamailio_trunk_cps{direction="inbound"}`), aggregated into FIXED, EQUAL-WIDTH buckets. THE BUCKET IS NO LONGER ALWAYS ONE HOUR — it auto-scales with the **Volume window** ($volwin) picker at the top of the board, and the title always names the bucket actually in force: **24h -> 1h bars (25 of them) · 7d -> 6h bars (29) · 30d -> 1d bars (31)**, because 168 hourly bars at 7d or 720 at 30d are unreadable on a wall. Bar height is an exact integer call count for whatever bucket is in force and does NOT rescale with the dashboard time picker — this panel ignores the picker and follows the **Volume window** picker instead (Grafana shows the window as a badge in this panel's header). Bars are drawn ENDING at their timestamp, so at the 24h setting a bar between the 13:00 and 14:00 gridlines is the 13:00-14:00 hour. Buckets tile exactly at EVERY window: the PromQL range and the query step are the same value (`increase(...[$__interval])`, and Grafana sets step = $__interval), and VictoriaMetrics' non-extrapolating increase() baselines each window on the last sample BEFORE it, so consecutive buckets neither double-count nor drop a call. A call landing within ~15s of a bucket boundary may be attributed to the next bar (it is counted at the scrape that observes it) — never twice, never zero. The stacked height IS the fleet total; the 'Total' series is hidden from the chart but kept in the legend and tooltip.

THE CURRENT, IN-PROGRESS BUCKET IS NEVER SHOWN — AND THAT BLIND SPOT GROWS WITH THE WINDOW. Grafana floors the query range down to whole buckets, so the newest bar is always the last COMPLETED bucket. At **24h** that costs up to 59 minutes: at 14:23 the rightmost bar is 13:00-14:00 and the last 23 minutes are not on this chart at all. At **7d** the bucket is 6 hours, so up to 6 hours of the most recent traffic is missing. At **30d** THE BUCKET IS A FULL DAY: the rightmost bar is YESTERDAY, and everything that has happened today — up to 23h59m of calls — is not plotted at all. A 30d wall that looks like it 'stopped a day ago' is CORRECT AND EXPECTED, not a traffic collapse, and the same goes for a missing newest bar at any window. The corollary is that the 7d and 30d settings can tell you NOTHING about today: for that, switch back to 24h, read the 'Calls — last 1h / last 24h' tiles (trailing windows ending now, so they DO include the current minute), or use 'CPS over time — by zone (1m rate)'. At every window these bars have no incident resolution — a 3-minute flood or a 20-minute outage just makes one bar slightly high or low. Bars are wall-clock aligned in every US timezone; across a DST change an hour label repeats (fall) or is skipped (spring), values still correct.

COUNTED EXACTLY ONCE PER CALL: the counter sits after `t_precheck_trans()` (absorbs INVITE retransmissions), after `bw_dedup` (482 Merged on the duplicate INVITEs Bandwidth sends from multiple edges), and after the `bw_cps` 503 backstop. On-net forwards are counted once at ingress and never re-counted per chain hop. Calls that later fail, are abandoned, or are hard-rejected on-net (603/483) still count as OFFERED — pair with 'Live ASR (5m)' to read completion. This is an offered-call count, NOT a billing figure, and 30d is a rolling 30 days, not a calendar month.

NOT INCLUDED — this is carrier ingress, not total platform volume: customer-originated SIP-trunk and API Calling traffic (`route[TRUNK_AUTH]` emits no counter today), runtime DB-admitted carriers (`carrier_trunks` — deliberately no metric, a DB-sourced carrier name is not a bounded label), and SIPp load-test ingress. `direction="outbound"` is deliberately NOT plotted: it is an ATTEMPT counter (the FreeSWITCH failover loop fires up to 8 bridge attempts per call) and the carrier B-leg of an RCF forward is the same call already counted inbound.

ACCURACY UNDER FAULTS: an SBC active/standby flip costs nothing (the ex-active's counter goes flat, the new active's climbs). A Kamailio container restart resets its counter to 0; that is corrected per-series before the zones are summed, losing at most 15s (one scrape) of that one SBC's calls in the bucket containing the restart. If a zone's link blips, vmagent replays its on-disk queue with original timestamps and VictoriaMetrics auto-resets its response cache on backfill — the affected bar SELF-CORRECTS upward on the next refresh, so an unexpectedly low recent bar may simply be data still in flight. A zone with NO BAR has stopped reporting entirely: that is missing data, not zero calls (an idle-but-healthy zone draws a zero-height bar, not a gap); at 7d/30d a bar can also be short simply because the metrics plane was not reporting for that whole bucket. Zone colours are deliberately NON-STATUS (blue / violet / teal): on this board green, amber and red always mean health, never a zone.

THIS PANEL WILL NOT MATCH THE 'Calls — last N' TILES ABOVE, AND THAT IS CORRECT. The tiles count a trailing window anchored on RIGHT NOW and include the period in progress; these bars cover only whole COMPLETED buckets and stop at the last bucket boundary — so the two differ at BOTH ends. Read the tiles for 'how many calls in the last N', and these bars for 'how did completed periods compare'. The legend's Total column sums the visible bars and will likewise not equal the tile.

The 'calls' value is a Kamailio SBC counter read from VictoriaMetrics; the 'minutes' value is summed out of the CDR database (PostgreSQL on the services VM) over the same trailing 30 days. Two independent planes with independent failure modes: either value can go blank or stale while the other stays healthy, so a disagreement between them is not by itself evidence of a traffic fault — establish which plane is still reporting before reading anything into the gap.

NOT PROPORTIONAL TO THE CALL COUNT — BY DESIGN. Minutes accrue only on ANSWERED calls (an unanswered call has no talk time), whereas the call count is OFFERED calls and deliberately includes everything that later failed, was abandoned, or was hard-rejected on-net. Minutes-per-call is therefore an answer-rate reading, not a data-quality reading: a low ratio means callers are not getting through — pair it with 'Live ASR (5m)' — and is never on its own a bug in this tile.

MINUTES — A DIFFERENT POPULATION FROM THE CALL COUNT BESIDE IT. DO NOT DIVIDE ONE BY THE OTHER. Minutes are total connected TALK TIME (answer_time -> end_time) summed across answered calls from the CDR database, rounded once to the nearest whole minute. Deliberately NOT `billable_ms`: rate_cdr() overwrites that column in place with a ring-INCLUSIVE duration floored at min_duration and rounded UP to the rate deck's increment, so a single admin rate call would silently change this number's meaning; it is also second-floored at ingest. Deliberately NOT `duration_ms` either, which includes ring time. This matches the talk-time convention already used by 'Voice · ACD — 1h' on the Home board — this tile is that panel's SUM. TALK TIME, NOT BILLED MINUTES: no per-call minimum and no billing increment, so it will not tie out against an Equinox invoice (RCF-V1 billing is estimates-only; the billing minute conversion happens downstream).

Scoped to direction='inbound' so it describes the SAME carrier-ingress traffic the call count does — customer-originated SIP-trunk and API Calling egress contribute no minutes here. It is still NOT proportional to the call count: (1) calls are OFFERED, minutes exist only for ANSWERED; (2) a CDR is written only at HANGUP, so calls in progress are already counted but contribute zero minutes until they end — material on the 1h tile, noise at 30d; (3) SIPp load-test ingress and runtime DB-admitted carriers produce CDRs but no Kamailio counter, so minutes inflate during a load test; (4) INVITEs rejected at the SBC before reaching FreeSWITCH are counted but produce no CDR. A low minutes-per-call ratio is an ASR story, not a bug.

Minutes are attributed to the window the call STARTED in, matching the call counter which increments at INVITE. A call that began before this window is excluded entirely — even talk time that fell inside it; a call that began inside contributes ALL its minutes, including talk continuing past the window's end. Calls come from Kamailio via VictoriaMetrics, minutes from Postgres CDRs — different stores, different write paths. CDR retention is 90 days (tighter than VictoriaMetrics' 12 months), never binding at 30d. A BLANK minutes value is a database or query error; zero traffic renders as 0.

targets.rawSql: SELECT ROUND(COALESCE(SUM(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (end_time - answer_time))), 0) / 60.0) AS minutes FROM cdrs WHERE leg IS DISTINCT FROM 'B' AND start_time > now() - interval '30 days' AND direction = 'inbound' AND answer_time IS NOT NULL AND end_time IS NOT NULL;

panels.description: Live signaling concurrency: sum(kamailio_dialog_active_dialogs) across the SBCs, honouring the Zone filter. This is SIP dialog state (what Kamailio is tracking) as opposed to media legs. One off-net call = 2 Kamailio dialogs (A-leg + B-leg) = 2 FreeSWITCH channels, so `gap` = dialogs − freeswitch_channels_total should sit near 0 (on-net calls push it negative). Amber when gap > 10: that is the vmalert SbcDialogLeak line (for: 2h30m — strictly longer than the 2h Kamailio dialog timeout, so post-failover ghost dialogs on the ex-active SBC never page; a gap that persists past 2h30m is a real leak). panels.title: Concurrency over time — media vs signaling (+ 30s peak)

One off-net call = 2 FS channels = 2 Kamailio dialogs, so `gap (dialogs − FS channels)` should hover near 0 (on-net calls push it negative; calls_active runs at ~half the channel count). The dashed amber line at 10 is the vmalert SbcDialogLeak threshold on the gap series (for: 2h30m). After an SBC failover the gap is EXPECTED to bulge and decay within the 2h dialog timeout (ghost dialogs on the ex-active SBC); a gap that stays above the line longer than that is a persistent leak → alert. The ONLY panel on this wall not sourced from VictoriaMetrics — it reads voip-cdr-pg, but the health view is poller-fresh (~3-15s), NOT call-derived. 🟢 UP (reachable from >=1 SBC) · 🔴 DOWN (dead on every SBC) · 🟠 STALE (no fresh probe in 90s). Proactive — a dead carrier shows even at zero call volume.

targets.rawSql: SELECT 'Bandwidth Dallas (primary)' AS carrier, CASE WHEN status IS NULL THEN 2 WHEN last_updated IS NULL OR last_updated < now() - interval '90 seconds' THEN 2 WHEN status = 'up' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS carrier_up FROM carrier_trunk_health WHERE duid = 'bw-dallas-primary';

SELECT 'Bandwidth LA (secondary)' AS carrier, CASE WHEN status IS NULL THEN 2 WHEN last_updated IS NULL OR last_updated < now() - interval '90 seconds' THEN 2 WHEN status = 'up' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS carrier_up FROM carrier_trunk_health WHERE duid = 'bw-la-secondary';

Rising shmem is an early warning of a dialog/tm leak or an under-provisioned SBC before it starts dropping calls.

panels.title: Oldest live channel — per FS
panels.description: Age of the OLDEST live channel on each FreeSWITCH: max by (freeswitch_node)(freeswitch_channel_max_age_seconds), honouring the Zone filter (ops_metrics.py, from `show channels as json` created_epoch). Legitimate RCF calls rarely run past 2h; amber at 7200s = a leg that most likely missed its BYE (post-failover teardown failure) and is waiting on RTP timeout / session timer. vmalert FsStaleChannels pages when freeswitch_channels_stale (count of legs > 2h) stays > 0 for 15m. Triage: `show channels` on that FS, `uuid_kill <uuid>` for a confirmed-stuck leg. 0 = idle.

panels.title: Dialogs per SBC — now
panels.description: Live signaling concurrency broken out per SBC: sum by (reporting_instance)(kamailio_dialog_active_dialogs), honouring the Zone filter. In steady state only the zone's ACTIVE SBC is non-zero (true active/standby). After a failover the EX-active SBC keeps the dialogs it was tracking as ghosts — nobody sends it the BYE — and they decay to 0 within the 2h Kamailio dialog timeout; that decay is normal. A non-zero count that persists on the standby beyond 2h, or a gap vs FS channels that persists (Active dialogs — now: `gap`), is a leak: vmalert SbcDialogLeak (for: 2h30m) covers it. No static amber line here on purpose — the baseline is the FS channel count, not a number; use the `gap` field on Active dialogs — now / the concurrency panel. Triage: `kamcmd dlg.list` on the SBC holding the dialogs, Homer for 481/408 on BYE.

panels.description:

With the active/standby NLB pairs a zone's whole load rides its ACTIVE SBC — steady state shows each zone's sbc-1 carrying everything and its sbc-2 flat at 0; the lines swap on failover/failback. This is the per-SBC processed-calls HISTORY that pairs with the election row up top (which answers 'who is active RIGHT NOW even at zero traffic'). Honours the Zone filter. Live from VictoriaMetrics.

list.name: volwin
list.label: Volume window
list.description: Time window for the 'Inbound calls' bar chart ONLY. It is read by that one panel's relative-time override (timeFrom) and by nothing else on this board: it does NOT move the dashboard time picker, and every other panel keeps the picker's range (default now-6h) and its own live semantics. The bar BUCKET auto-scales with the choice so the chart always draws ~30 readable bars instead of 168 or 720 hairlines: 24h -> 1h bars (24) · 7d -> 6h bars (28) · 30d -> 1d bars (30). Coarser buckets enlarge the chart's blind spot — the current, in-progress bucket is never drawn, so at 30d the newest bar is YESTERDAY. CAVEAT: a panel relative-time override only applies while the DASHBOARD time range is relative; if someone drag-zooms the wall or picks an absolute range, this picker silently stops applying and the bar chart follows the picker instead. Reset the picker to a relative range (e.g. Last 6 hours) to get it back.
